questions.question:

An extremely fat person sitting all alone in a room
A wild untamed animal left to wander astray
A pretty affair which is kept a secret

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **An obvious issue left unaddressed due to its sensitivity**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• "**Elephant in the room**" means that there is an obvious problem or difficult situation that people do not want to talk about.

 
 
• Example - *We all sat sipping our tea quietly, no one wanting to bring up the **elephant in the room** about Joel's expulsion from the college.*
 
 
 
• So, it is clear that the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom "**Elephant in the room**" is **"An obvious issue left unaddressed due to its sensitivity"**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

If he works harder, he g__ot__ better results.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **will get**

__
 
• Replace **'got' **with **'will get'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• The above incomplete sentence is in the mood of a **Conditional Sentence**. After filling up the gap the sentence has turned into an example of a **Probable Conditional Sentence.**
 
• A probable Conditional Sentence means it can happen in reality. Here **'better result' **will happen **if hard work is done by him**.
 
• In the Probable Conditional Sentence** 'if clause' **is written in **Simpler Present Tense** and the next part of the sentence should be written in **Simple Future Tense.**
 
• **Example - **
 
 
• **​*****If **the downpour continues, the match **will be** cancelled.*
 
 

*​*Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4.**

**Corrected sentence:** *If he works harder, he **will get__** better results.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Their dog is / more better / trained than / our dog.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **more better**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Replace **"more better" **with **"much better"** to make the sentence correct.
 
• Because the **comparative form of good is better**, we can't say **"more better."**
 
• The usage of **“much better”** is absolutely correct. **Better is a comparative degree of good **and we can use** "much" **with the comparative degree.
 
• So then, we can say
 
 
• **"She's much better than he is" **
 
 
 
• In very rare cases we can say 
 
 
• **"She's much more good than he is"** 
 
• but **"She's much more better than he is" **is incorrect.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2.**

**Corrected sentence: ***Their dog is **much better** trained than our dog. *

2) Granted: To give something as an entitlement or favor, without necessarily being based on a competitive process or meeting specific requirements. The thing granted is usually given as a right or privilege that is expected or deserved by the recipient.

 Example: The government granted tax exemptions to new businesses.

 
3) Gifted: To give something to someone as a present or without any expectation of payment or compensation in return. The thing gifted is usually given out of generosity or to show affection or appreciation towards the recipient.

 Example: She gifted her friend a handmade quilt for her birthday.

 
4) Awarded: To give something to someone based on their merit, qualifications, or performance in a competitive process. The thing awarded is usually earned by the recipient based on their successful completion of a project, presentation, competition, or similar event.

 Example: The scholarship was awarded to the student with the highest academic performance.

 
It is important to note that while these words may have some overlap in their definitions, they each have their own nuances and connotations that make them more appropriate in certain contexts.

 
 
• As per the meaning of the given words. **Awarded **is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Corrected sentence:** *The government **awarded **__the contract for 100 low-floor buses to an automobile manufacturer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**

 
• An **award **is usually something given by one person to another for some sort of achievement.
 
• **Rewards **aren’t always given by someone, and they don’t necessarily have to do with achievement.
